name: Hot-water start
summary: Start with hot water so the coffee never sits and cooks on the stove. Stop early and cool the base.

grind.description: Fine, about table salt (finer than drip, coarser than espresso)

steps.title: Heat the water
steps.instruction: Boil water in a kettle, then take it off the heat.
steps.why: Hot water in the base shortens the time the grounds sit above a flame, which avoids a scorched, metallic taste.

steps.title: Fill and load
steps.instruction: Pour the hot water into the base up to just under the safety valve. Fill the basket level, with no tamping, and wipe stray grounds off the rim.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.instruction: Screw the top on snugly using a towel, because the base is hot.
steps.why: A loose seal leaks steam and pressure.

steps.title: Brew on moderate heat
steps.instruction: Set it on moderate heat with the lid open and the handle clear of the flame. Watch for the coffee stream.
steps.why: Gentle heat gives a slow, even flow. Fast, spitting flow means the heat is too high.

steps.title: Stop when the stream blondes
steps.instruction: When the stream turns pale, like yellow honey, and starts to sputter, take it off the heat and close the lid.
steps.why: The last of the stream is the most bitter part.

steps.title: Cool the base
steps.instruction: Wrap the base in a cold wet towel or run it briefly under cold water, then pour.
steps.why: Stops extraction right away, which preserves sweetness.

sources.title: Stumptown: How to brew coffee in a moka pot
